description: baseline: RandomForest(20 trees, depth 10) on speed_mph, grade_percent, miles
hypothesis: establishes the reference point every later experiment is measured against; no prior session exists in this tree
observation: rmse=0.013345, trip_rmse=0.003037 in 7.3s of the 600s budget
reasoning: the run uses ~1% of the time budget, so the baseline is almost certainly capacity-limited rather than data-limited — there is room for far larger models and richer features before the budget binds

hypothesis: the baseline forest is capacity-limited (it uses 1% of the time budget), so deeper trees should fit the heavy-tailed target better and lower both metrics
reasoning: depth 10 was already past the useful point for 3 features — the extra depth memorizes noise in the regen tail rather than signal, so the baseline is feature-limited, not depth-limited; unused time budget is not evidence of under-capacity

description: n_estimators 20 -> 100 (Pareto-better but discarded on inference cost)
hypothesis: more trees is variance reduction rather than capacity, a different knob from exp1 depth, so it should help or tie on both metrics
observation: both metrics improved but only by 0.03% (rmse 0.013345 -> 0.013341, trip_rmse 0.003037 -> 0.003036) at 5x the trees and 2x the fit time
reasoning: technically Pareto-dominant but the gain is noise-level while the inference cost is 5x per link traversal, which domain.md names as a competing objective — rejected on the cost/simplicity criterion, and it confirms exp1 that the 3-feature model is feature-limited, not model-limited

description: add one-link lookback feature prev_speed_mph (first link of journey filled with 0)
hypothesis: domain.md names acceleration as the dominant unmeasured driver of energy use and permits one backward link; the previous links speed is the only available proxy, so it should cut link error substantially
observation: rmse fell 31.3% (0.013345 -> 0.009164) while trip_rmse fell only 1.55% (0.003037 -> 0.002990); both improved so this Pareto-dominates
reasoning: the lookback is by far the biggest lever found so far, confirming acceleration was the missing signal; the lopsided split is the key insight — acceleration and braking errors largely cancel when summed along a journey, so trip totals were already near-right and the gain is almost entirely link-level precision
